assessment.rationale: Good fit for the envelope-independence pressure because the envelope keeps meaning in the payload protocol, preserves exact bytes, and fails unknown pCIDs explicitly. The main limits are that it does not actually demonstrate a CAS-backed group-session payload across alternate envelopes, the base envelope is unsigned, and the draft has a few signature-related ambiguities.
strengths: Opaque payload plus no speculative parsing keeps group-session meaning above the envelope layer.
Deterministic CBOR exact bytes make storage, forwarding, and cross-experiment comparison straightforward.
Unknown-pCID store/forward with explicit unsupported results supports sparse knowledge and visible failure.
The spec avoids a central pCID registry and does not claim canonical-winner status.
weaknesses: It does not demonstrate the same CAS-backed group-session payload under multiple envelope variants.
The base envelope is unsigned, so authorship and integrity depend on other layers.
The draft is unfrozen and has no freeze history yet.
Some text references signature-related slots or fields even though this variant's base shape is [pcid, payload].
risks: Transport or payload conventions could still reintroduce envelope-dependent semantics in practice.
If higher layers do not provide robust signatures and replay controls, tampering and attribution gaps remain.
Long-term pCID-to-spec resolution may be brittle unless the referenced spec artifacts are durably mirrored.
open_questions: Can one CAS-backed group-session payload be wrapped by sibling envelope variants with identical observable semantics and audit records?
Which layer supplies authorship, integrity, and anti-replay guarantees for this scenario?
How will a 100-year reader resolve pCID-to-spec meaning without relying on the current repo layout?
Should the draft remove or clarify the signature-slot references in this unsigned v0 variant?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.
